design_objections: Segmentation is coupled to the error being measured. Points are assigned to faces via the registered S_k labels within 1.5-2 mm and 15-20 degrees, and S_k assumes nominal angles on formed bends. A 2 degree error on a 300 mm flange moves the tip by about 10 mm, so exactly the defective flanges drop out of the gate and come back UNKNOWN or MISSING instead of FAIL. The claim that 'angle and flange length depend on the pose only through segmentation' hides this. Fix: walk the flange tree from the datum panel, fit each child flange plane locally with a hinge-constrained or articulated fit and theta free, and grow the region by plane fit rather than by distance to nominal.

Using P+1 rigid stage templates for registration repeats the rigid-to-wrong-shape problem at smaller scale: formed bends are still frozen at nominal. Trimmed ICP 'on the visible overlap only' will fit the datum island under every hypothesis and trim away the flanges that disagree, so the robust residual is a weak stage discriminator. The per-bend normal-turn test is the real signal. It needs only one datum registration and a sequential formed/unformed test per hinge, which is cheaper and avoids P+1 times the symmetric-pose candidates.

The runtime budget ignores multiplicity. Each of the P+1 stage hypotheses also needs the symmetric or mirrored coarse-pose candidates the design itself requires, so registration is (P+1) x symmetric candidates x ICP, not P+1 x 1 s. Dense scans (the pipeline branches at 550k-650k+ points) also need normal estimation at full resolution for section metrology, which is unbudgeted. The 30 s P95 is a target, not something derived from evidence.

Marking flange lengths that end on a not-yet-formed bend as NOT_APPLICABLE, 'developed length informational only', discards the most actionable mid-sequence check. The backgauge-set distance from the just-formed bend's OML to the far edge, across still-flat material, is measurable and has a stage-specific nominal from S_k or the shop flat. Catching backgauge error before later bends is the main value of scanning incomplete parts. It should be a toleranced characteristic.

'Flange length per side' measured at 5-11 stations by median, from a boundary fit of the free edge, is ill-defined for tapered, notched, relieved or holed flanges and for flanges whose far boundary is another bend over only part of the span. Drawings dimension specific features. The operator-tagged general_measurements (bend_pair/points, vendor_setup_service.py:45-56) and drawing callouts should be the primary length characteristics, with per-bend station lengths as a diagnostic. The design puts them last (B.7).

OML from 'inner surface + t' uses nominal thickness, and on a fixtured robotic cell only one side is visible for alternating up/down flanges. Thickness tolerance and edge dropout bias then enter every second flange length. The design should measure t where both skins are seen, or carry the nominal-t uncertainty in U explicitly per side.

The stage hypothesis space (prefixes at מהלך boundaries only) conflicts with the existing UI, where completed_steps is per bend and can split a group. It also cannot represent the out-of-order or skipped bends the design wants to detect, except through the offline residual lane. A per-bend formed/unformed decode constrained softly by order would cover both.

Declaring whole SKUs UNSUPPORTED at onboarding for 'spline (49001000)' is an overreach. 49001000 refused only full-skin UNFOLD because of a B-spline surface (CURRENT_STATUS.md:511). Its 5 straight bends are fully scan-supported (V11 analysis:38-41). Unsupported status should apply per feature, not per part.

Method A's flat strip of length alpha(Ri+K·t), with an unknown K, puts about ±1 mm into every unformed-bend stage model. That is the same order as the proposed flange-length P95 gate of 0.3 mm. Without a shop K (or one back-computed from a bound real flat against the folded CAD per bend), stage-model geometry cannot support length decisions on incomplete parts. The design should derive K at onboarding when a flat is bound, not just 'flag' the uncertainty.

The 'fix the cylinder-axis locus first' advice should also apply to the production per-bend position characteristic. The proposed OML virtual sharp sits sqrt(2)·R from the axis at 90 degrees. The surface-referenced labels and the scorer's 4 mm limit were built around different loci, so the line matcher is not a valid secondary check until the line convention is signed.

The Jev hook adds an external network dependency and scope the user did not ask for. Since the bend list comes from the confirmed setup, it should be cut from the production design document rather than kept as three advisory hooks.
verdict: Most of the synthesis holds up and its central thesis is right. Every F1 number measures bend-line localization only. Flange length is unmeasured and has no truth. CAD helped only as a conservative union (0.458 vs 0.365 on matched Gold11). The cylinder-axis locus defect is real. The setup draft has no consumer. Spot-checks confirmed the Hungarian 5°/4 mm/0.6 matcher, blind 3/12 at P95 46.3 s, the non-blind evaluator, the degrees-as-mm datum threshold, the arg-max tip distance, the Poisson-binomial count, V11's use of line_start/SUPPORT 3.0, the 133/472 module counts, 120/127, and the 33 dangling symlinks. But it has real errors. It attributes the 0.327 Gold37 score to V51; that number is the structured-union lane, and V51 scored 0.634 there in development. It misses that the count promotion is a silent no-op, because latest.json points into /Users/idant. It says no partial-scan engine, evaluation or stage labels existed, but Era 0 had partial branches, a sequence-continuity prior and expected-completed labels on 16-21 scans. It says no engine measures flange length, but qc_engine's 'flange' dimension lane and cad_guided's nominal flange lengths exist. It overstates auto-scale, and it treats 94% of bends as 94% of CADs. The production design's direction is sound: compile the CAD and setup once per SKU, measure each scan per characteristic, and make UNKNOWN or REVIEW explicit. Its handling of incomplete parts is the weak point. Nominal-angle rigid stage templates combined with a distance-to-nominal segmentation gate make defective flanges come back UNKNOWN. The design ignores the runtime's 0.55 fitness hard-fail on partial scans. It assumes a per-scan stage declaration that does not exist (completed_steps is per SKU and counted in bends). It throws away the backgauge length on mid-sequence parts, and it has no partially-formed or multi-hit state. Revise it toward the setup plan's articulated, hinge-constrained per-flange fit walked from the datum. Use drawing-anchored length characteristics. Derive K from bound real flats. Use the physical 'BEFORE BENDING 11979003' blank scan and the existing repeat scans now. Drop or quarantine Jev.
